title: Client Circuit Breaker & Warmup Notes
content:
Purpose
---
Freeform scratchpad for designing a client-side circuit breaker + warmup sequence for small-scale canaries of the new model-packing runtime (v0.9.3). Goal is to reduce noisy 5xx spikes, protect downstream client libraries, and ensure steady token-latency distribution during ramp. NOT a formal runbook — use this to capture heuristics and test notes before we formalize a playbook.

Context
---
- Target release: runtime packaging + batching changes (v0.9.3).
- Primary risk: transient KV-cache invalidations causing 4xx/5xx burst when traffic first hits canary nodes.
- Secondary risk: client throttling/backpressure cascades causing long-tail latency.
- Canary size target: staged cohorts under SDK/edge clients, starting at 0.5% of global traffic.

High-level approach
---
1) Client-side circuit breaker (CSCB) layered with server-side safety: client limits open requests + immediate failover to host fallback.
2) Warmup cohorts: small cohorts with initial low QPS + conservative timeouts to prime caches and kernels.
3) Instrumentation gate: only increase cohort size if metrics pass for two consecutive windows.

Client circuit breaker design (proposed)
---
- Modes: CLOSED -> PROBATION -> OPEN -> HALF-OPEN -> CLOSED
- Key metrics tracked per client region: consecutive 5xx count, 95th latency, percent short-circuit (local cb rejects), error budget burn rate.
- Thresholds (initial, conservative):
  - PROBATION after 3 consecutive 5xx within 60s window
  - OPEN after 6 consecutive 5xx within 3m window or if 95th latency > 1200ms sustained for 2 windows
  - HALF-OPEN after 5m cool-down; allow 5 probe requests per minute to judge health
- Probation behavior: reduce concurrency by 50%, increase per-request timeout by +300ms, route new requests to stable model variants when possible.
- Open behavior: short-circuit with graceful fallback (cached completion or lower-capability model) and emit metric tag cb_open=true.
- Observability: every state transition emits event to telemetry with request-sample (trace id).

Warmup cohort plan
---
Stage A (priming):
- Cohort size: 0.5% of traffic for 30m window.
- Client config: concurrency cap 2, per-request timeout 2s, circuit breaker probation thresholds doubled (very tolerant while priming).
- Server action: keep kernels hot (no preemption), pre-populate KV prefix cache for popular prompts (simulate warm inputs).
- Success criteria: 95th latency <= 700ms, error rate <0.1% absolute increase vs baseline, no more than 1 circuit breaker open event.

Stage B (steady warm):
- Ramp to 2% over 60m if Stage A passes two windows.
- Client config: concurrency cap 4, timeout 1.5s, normal CB thresholds.
- Additional checks: memory alloc patterns stable (no >15% variance), GPU utilization within expected band.

Stage C (validation):
- Ramp to 10% over next 3h if Stage B good for 2 consecutive windows.
- Run targeted smoke tests from canary cohort: heavy KV-churn, long context-length requests, function-calling sequences.

Metrics and gating windows
---
- Window length: 5m evaluation; require 2 consecutive windows passing to move to next stage.
- Primary gates: 95th latency, error rate increase, cpu/gpu anomaly, CB open count.
- Automated gating thresholds (first pass):
  - 95th latency increase <= +20% from baseline
  - Error rate increase <= +0.5 percentage points absolute
  - Circuit breaker opens <= 2 per window
  - No new class of 5xx signatures (e.g., RLModelFailure)

Smoke test checklist for each cohort
---
- [ ] synthetic latency sweeps (short -> long contexts)
- [ ] KV-heavy sequences to exercise cache priming
- [ ] concurrency spike test (burst 3x expected per-client QPS for 30s)
- [ ] function-calling with large tool payload to test marshalling layer
- [ ] verify fallback response correctness (cached vs degraded model)

Rollback & fallback hooks (client play)
---
- Immediate local fallback: serve cached completion or call fallback model variant (downgrade to small-llm) when CB open.
- Centralized rollback: if server-side alarms trigger (cascade rate >= threshold) we issue traffic pin to stable model and send canary cohort to safe route.
- Emergency: force clients to short-circuit all non-essential enriched calls (tool-calls, images) and preserve minimal text completion traffic.

Operational run commands (notes)
---
- quick pin to stable model (CLI): rcli routing pin --model stable-v0.9 --cohort=canary
- throttle cohort: rcli traffic update --cohort=canary --pct=0.1
- query cb state for a region (dev helper): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://telemetry.internal/api/cb-state?region=us-west-2

Open questions & TODOs
---
- Durable client config propagation: how quickly do client SDKs get updated thresholds? Need a config TTL plan.
- Should we ship a binary toggle to flip CB into "learning" mode for first 24h? Pros/cons.
- Determine final numeric thresholds with SRE after a dry-run on staging.
- Add test harness to inject synthetic 5xx signatures and validate CB transitions.

Notes from experiments (scratch)
---
- 2026-01-14: quick stress on staging - cold KV causes 400s for a subset: increasing probation window from 60s->180s reduced noise but hid real flapping. Need careful balance.
- 2026-02-02: Maya's priming idea (prewarm by replaying QPS 10 mins prior) reduced first-minute 95th by ~18% in local test. Consider adding prewarm replay as opt-in.

Next steps (practical)
---
- [ ] Draft SDK config flags and default values for client CB (Harper)
- [ ] Schedule staging dry-run with SRE and Maya (target window: next Thursday 10–12 PST)
- [ ] Implement telemetry event contract for CB transitions (Samir)
- [ ] Bake warmup replay tool into staging harness (Rui)

Appendix: quick defaults (for discussion)
---
- client.default.timeout=1500ms
- client.default.concurrency=4
- client.cb.probation_threshold=3-in-60s
- client.cb.open_threshold=6-in-3m
- client.cb.half_open_probes=5-per-minute

End of scratchpad
